images.title: Full turn and half turn
images.purpose: Show the two turns side by side: a child who turns until facing the start way again (full turn, a complete circle drawn by the free foot) and a child who turns until facing the opposite way (half turn, a half-moon), and a minute hand that comes back to the initial position.
images.composition: Three equal panels in a row, a full turn on the ground, a half turn on the ground and a full turn of the minute hand, each with one caption underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Three panels, each 420 by 520 px with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and a very pale cream #FFF8E7 fill, at x 50 to 470, x 518 to 938 and x 986 to 1406, all y 110 to 630. PANEL 1: seen from above, a flat ground ring (a thin grey #6B7280 circle, 240 px across, centre (260, 330)) with exactly 1 child shown as a round head and shoulders (a dark outline circle 60 px with a teal #0072B2 shirt-colour shoulder shape) at the centre; a teal start arrow 100 px long from the centre pointing straight up; the free foot's path is a complete circle drawn in amber #E69F00 (6 px line) over the ring, with one curved amber arrowhead on the circle showing it goes round and ends back at the top. PANEL 2: the same ring and the same child at centre (728, 330), the teal start arrow pointing straight up; the free foot's path is a half-moon, only the right half of the ring drawn in amber (6 px line) from the top, down the right side to the bottom, with an amber arrowhead at the bottom; the child's own arrow now points straight down in amber (100 px). PANEL 3: a round clock face (a thin dark circle 240 px across, centre (1196, 330)) with the numbers 12, 3, 6 and 9 inside at their places, a short dark minute hand pointing at 12 in teal, and a complete amber circle arrow round the face ending back at the hand. Captions under the panels, centred at y 690 in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (34 px, bold): Full turn: back at the start under panel 1, Half turn: facing the opposite way under panel 2, and The minute hand makes a full turn under panel 3. Nothing else in the frame.
labels: Full turn: back at the start
Half turn: facing the opposite way
The minute hand makes a full turn

images.takeaway: A full turn brings you back to the start; a half turn leaves you facing the opposite way.
images.description: Three panels: a ring with a complete circle for a full turn, a ring with a half-moon for a half turn, and a clock with the minute hand going round to where it started.
images.context: Concept image for Full Turn and Half Turn. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (Ashutosh's complete circle, Sahana's half-moon and the minute hand that comes back to the initial position) and shows the concept's own example of a child turning on a ring.
images.teaching_notes: Trace the circle and the half-moon with a finger. The slip to watch is thinking a full turn means no turn at all.

image_decisions.why: The ring with a complete circle, the ring with a half-moon and the clock together show what a full turn and a half turn look like.
